title: Why Unused Drains Smell Like Sewer Gas
description: A persistent sewer smell coming from a rarely used bathroom or basement floor drain often stems from a dry P-trap rather than a broken pipe. The P-trap holds a standing water seal that acts as a barrier blocking hazardous sewer gases from entering living spaces. When a fixture goes unused for extended periods, ambient evaporation slowly depletes this water barrier. Once the water level drops below the trap dip, sewer odors pass freely into the room. Running water for a few seconds re-establishes the liquid seal, immediately resolving the odor issue without complex repairs.

Why Unused Drains Smell Like Sewer Gas

A persistent sewer smell coming from a rarely used bathroom or basement floor drain often stems from a dry P-trap rather than a broken pipe. The P-trap holds a standing water seal that acts as a barrier blocking hazardous sewer gases from entering living spaces. When a fixture goes unused for extended periods, ambient evaporation slowly depletes this water barrier. Once the water level drops below the trap dip, sewer odors pass freely into the room. Running water for a few seconds re-establishes the liquid seal, immediately resolving the odor issue without complex repairs.
